Blackhearts.descripcion:
Originally formed as an elite anti-terrorist unit known as the Seventy-seventh Special Operations Group within the Star League's Special Armed Services. Their tradition of leaving playing cards on the bodies of their victims along with their brutal reputation lead the common SLDF soldiers to give them the nickname "The Blackhearts." 

Many members of the original Seventy-seventh SOG joined Alexander Kerensky's exodus from known space. Those that stayed behind adopted their former nickname and opted to work as independent mercenaries after the Star League's collapse. Excelling at small-unit tactics and night-time operations.

BrionsLegion.descripcion:
Colonel Pythonius Brion and his legion have only been active since 3013, but have already gathered a reputation for bad luck and constantly being at the wrong place at the wrong time. 

The Legion suffered significant losses on Tancredi II under their first employer, House Kurita. Their increasingly dire financial situation has made the Legion quick to accept contracts with anyone who would offer them work. While scrappy and somewhat cowardly, it is rumored that, for whatever reason, ComStar and the MRB have begun to take a great interest in Brion and the success of his legion.

CraterCobras.descripcion:
Formed as Baldwin's Cobras Heavy Brigade from the remnants of several SLDF regular army units that declined to join Kerensky's exodus, the Cobra's fondness for heavy artillery earned them the nickname "Crater Makers." This nickname amused the Cobras so much that they would eventually rename themselves the "Crater Cobras."

Now led by Col. Richard Westrick, the Crater Cobras have gained a reputation for getting the job done no matter the odds stacked against them.  Including participating in First Prince Hanse Davion's successful raid on Halstead Station in 3013.

EridaniLightHorse.descripcion:
One of the largest and oldest mercenary units active in the Inner Sphere. The Eridani Light Horse was initially formed as a large Star League regimental combat team. After the Star League's collapse, the Light Horse attempted to stay neutral as the First Succession War erupted around them. But Jinjiro Kurita's role in the Kentares massacre forced the Light Horse to reconsider its position. After escaping Combine space, they took refuge in the Free Worlds League agreeing to work with the League as mercenaries.

Nowadays the Light Horse's size has allowed the unit to subcontract out individual battalions to multiple employers throughout the Inner Sphere. Provided they are never asked to fight their own.

FilthyLucre.descripcion:
"Whose mouths must be stopped, who subvert whole houses, teachings things which they ought not, for filthy lucre's sake." 

Titus 1:11 King James Bible

Never ones for taste or decency, the Filthy Lucre has operated out of the Lyran Commonwealth since the First Succession War. With many family members attending prestigious Lyran MechWarrior academies, the Filthy Lucre use their ties to the Commonwealth's top academies as a way of scalping graduates to use as fresh recruits. Enticing them to join them in the private sector to earn that filthy lucre for themselves working for anyone willing to pay for their services.

GrayDeathLegion.descripcion:
In 3024 a small mercenary unit known as Carlyle's Commandos was ambushed by Oberon Confederation pirates on Trell I. Killing the unit's CO and many of its members. The survivors of the Commandos rallied around Grayson Death Carlyle, son of the Commando's former CO Durant Carlyle, and formed an ad-hoc militia unit, The First Trellwan Lancers.

After discovering a plot by Duke Haasid Ricol of the Draconis Combine to conquer Trell, the Trellwan Lancers staged a prolonged guerrilla war that ended with Duke Ricol ejected from the system. With Trell now resecured for the Lyran Commonwealth, Grayson Carlyle has reformed the First Trellwan Lancers into a new mercenary company under his command. 

They now call themselves the Gray Death Legion.

GreggsLongstriders.descripcion:
A belligerent veteran of the famed Wolf's Dragoons, Gregg Car would eventually part ways with the Dragoons in 3022 along with like-minded disgruntled former Dragoons and Tamar Pact MechWarriors that rallied around his leadership to form a new mercenary unit.  

Although Car no longer associates himself with the Dragoons, he is not above leveraging his former employer's reputation as a way of inflating the rates of the MechWarriors on his payroll well above the market average. His exorbitant rates have allowed him to retain top talent, but at the cost of the unit plunging ever deeper into debt.

HansensRoughRiders.descripcion:
A former House Davion line unit that fled the Federated Suns in 2961 over fears that they would not survive an ongoing purge of units with questionable loyalty to the AFFS high command.  Initially taking refuge in the Lyran Commonwealth before relocating to the Free Worlds League, the Roughriders adopted a rough-and-tumble mercenary persona that's earned them a reputation of always being willing to plunge themselves into the thickest battles and emerging victorious. 

This reputation has made the unit media darlings for news outlets that cover the exploits of mercenary commands. Particularly in the Lyran Commonwealth. Which has led to the Roughriders becoming one of the most well-known and well-liked mercenary units throughout the entire Inner Sphere.

HarlocksWarriors.descripcion:
Prior to the Second Succession War, Jinjiro Kurita emptied the Combine's prisons and penal camps assembling three regiments worth of convicts, undesirables, and unproductives placed under the command of disgraced officers and equipped with 'Mechs and equipment on the verge of becoming scrap metal. These "Chain Gang Regiments" were ordered to assault a number of Steiner and Davion border worlds, those that were successful in their mission would earn redemption and their freedom. While throwing many systems into disarray these suicidal chain gang missions mostly served House Kurita as a way to rid itself of its rabble. 

Survivors of the chain gang raid of Kobe in 2825 would go on to form the Harlock Warriors mercenary command. Through sheer grit and determination over nearly 200 years of service, Harlock's Warriors have scraped through situations that would have broken lesser mercenary commands. Proving themselves among the toughest survivors to ever take up the mercenary life.

KellHounds.descripcion:
As children, Morgan and Patrick Kell would often terrorize their neighbor's flock of sheep. Amused by these antics, their cousin and future husband to Archon Katrina Steiner, Arthur Luvon, dubbed the two brothers the Kell Hounds. A name that would follow Morgan and Patrick into adulthood. 

After Arthur Luvon's death, the Kell brothers would form the Kell Hounds mercenary command using endowments left to them from their late cousin. With familial ties to both the Steiner royal family and the Arc-Royal MechWorks factories, the Kell Hounds quickly built up a reputation for being one of the most highly trained and well-equipped mercenary commands in the entire Inner Sphere.

LindonsCompany.descripcion:
Originally a part of Reilly's Armored Cavalry mercenary command, the unit was destroyed when their employers, the Draconis Combine, sent them on a diversionary raid without their promised DCMS support. The few MechWarriors that survived the ordeal rallied around Captain Owen Lindon to flee Combine space and reformed the unit under a new name. Lindon's Company. 

Although currently, only a company-sized unit comprised of only Light and Medium 'Mechs, Lindon's MechWarriors are career mercenaries with generations worth of experience among its members. Making them a highly reliable outfit to those that retain their services.

McCarronsArmoredCavalry.descripcion:
Widely considered one of the largest and most successful mercenary units in existence, McCarron's Armored Cavalry, also known as "The Big Mac," is one of the only mercenary companies that has worked for and fought against all five of the Great Houses of the Inner Sphere since the unit's formation in 2930. 

Widely known for combined arms tactics across their six active regiments, The Big Mac's Armored divisions have a reputation of being just as deadly as the BattleMech regiments they support.

Their latest employer, House Liao, has provided extensive support to the unit. Granting generous pay rates and gifting MAC a base of operations that the Chancellor hopes will become the unit's permanent home. A prospect McCarron seems to be warming up to given their host's generous compensation package.

MobileFire.descripcion:
Created as an exclusive armored vehicle and artillery support command, Mobile Fire's track record of success has recently led the LCAF to sponsor their growth by gifting them a number of Battlemechs to expand their command. 

Although grateful for this gift, after over 100 years of experience focused on the asymmetric nature of tank vs. 'Mech combat, Mobile Fire's command staff is struggling to adapt to the nuances of BattleMech tactics. Over the past few years, they have gained ground and have taken independent contracts aimed at giving their 'Mech divisions more direct experience, but with no formal 'Mech training, Mobile Fire's leadership is well aware that they have a long way to go in developing their BattleMech competency.

NorthwindHighlanders.descripcion:
Pre-dating the formation of the Star League by centuries, the Northwind Highlanders are one of the oldest military organizations in all of human colonized space. Formed from the remnants of the Highlanders, the final members of Scotland's independent military, they joined Clan Stuart in colonizing the system of Northwind. Building their new home to preserve the proud traditions of Scotland and Terra as humanity began migrating into the stars.

Five centuries later, the Northwind Highlanders are an elite mercenary unit scorned. Ejected from Northwind by House Davion during the Second Succession War, the Highlanders have vowed to one day take back Northwind and work tirelessly as one of the most elite mercenaries in all of the Inner Sphere to see their dream of returning home realized.

TheBadDream.descripcion:
Originally a line unit of the Capellan Confederation that fell on bad times, the under-strengthed Bad Dream was abandoned by the CCAF during a failed raid into the Draconis Combine during the First Succession War. Turning to the mercenary life to survive, the Bad Dream has since stabilized after finding steady employment with both House Kurita and House Davion. 

The Bad Dream has since diversified its clientele and has actively been pursuing work across the Inner Sphere.  Although their approach to combat is often criticized as "by the books" and "unimaginative," there is no denying their no-nonsense attitude towards their craft has left a mostly positive impression on every command the unit has worked with.

Thumpers.descripcion:
Created as a demonstration unit to market the sales of Defiance Industries' assault 'Mechs, the Thumpers were initially well received, but eventually, Defiance attempted to disband the unit for poor performance. Rather than disband, the Thumpers' MechWarriors launched a successful buyout of the organization. 

Since the buyout, the Thumpers have uniquely managed themselves as a pure business venture with each of its senior officers becoming shareholders and serving on the company's board of directors with voting power based on their accumulated shares. Additionally, the officer that holds the most company shares becomes both the CEO and commanding officer of Thumpers LLC. 

While this structure has made the Thumpers a unique business oddity, it has not done the Thumpers any favors when it comes to successfully managing military operations. As a whole, the unit is often poorly regarded for any work beyond garrison duties.

WacoRangers.descripcion:
Wayne Waco began his career as an exceptional MechWarrior in the Capellan Confederation's First Tau Ceti Rangers. When House Liao disbanded the unit in 3007 Wayne and many of his former rangers went mercenary forming the Waco Rangers from the remnants of the First Tau Ceti.

What started as a promising mercenary career quickly went south when one of the Ranger's first assignments pitted them against Wolf's Dragoons. An encounter that ended tragically with Wayne's son John crushed under the foot of a Zeta Battalion Stalker. This act and the subsequent drama around John's death caused the elder Waco to declare a blood feud against the Dragoons. Refusing employment with any state that also employed the Dragoons and swore to enact vengeance against the Dragoons for maliciously murdering his son. 

Waco's all-consuming obsession with vengeance has made him unpredictable and temperamental, much to the detriment of his mercenary command. Unfortunately earning his unit the derisive nickname of the "Wacko Rangers."

WolfsDragoons.descripcion:
Unquestionably the most elite and famous mercenary unit currently operating in the Inner Sphere. The tales of Wolf's Dragoons exploits have elevated the likes of Jaimie Wolf, Natasha Kerensky, and J. Elliot Jamison into the stuff of legend. Only rivaled by the wild theories as to the group's mysterious origin. 

No one had heard of the Dragoons prior to the group materializing at the jump point for the remote Federated Suns border world of Delos on the 11th of April 3005 seeking asylum. Appearing out of nowhere with a heavily escorted flotilla of spacecraft, including a massive orbital factory of unknown design and five full regiments of pristine BattleMechs. Their sudden appearance caused outright panic in Delos IV until a delegation from First Prince Ian Davion successfully negotiated asylum for the Dragoon's families in exchange for a five-year mercenary contract with the mysterious group.

Since their sudden appearance, the mystery surrounding the group has only grown as nearly every campaign uncovers yet more questions about the Dragoons. Most recently, the discovery of previously unknown 'Mechs exclusively fielded by the group such as the massive Annihilator and Marauder II.
